claims.explanation: AZD7762 is a Chk1/Chk2 inhibitor that selectively kills tumor cells with a defective G1 DNA-damage checkpoint, forcing reliance on Chk1-dependent S/G2 arrest and homologous recombination repair; cells with intact p53-mediated G1 arrest or robust Chk1 signaling survive, while those with p53 loss, high replication stress, or impaired HR are sensitized. The virtual-cell response (down CDK1/CCNA2/BIRC5, up ERBB3/FOXO4) is consistent with mitotic catastrophe and checkpoint abrogation rather than a single kinase off-target.

features.basis: Loss of G1 checkpoint creates Chk1 dependence; p53-mutant lines radiosensitized more than WT (PMID 20233881, 22446188)
High Chk1 activation drives S/G2 arrest and survival after DNA damage (PMID 22117197)
AZD7762 inhibits Rad51 focus formation and homologous recombination; high HR capacity protects (PMID 20501833)
CDK1/CCNA2 downregulation in virtual cell indicates mitotic catastrophe from checkpoint loss
CDK1 downregulation in virtual cell reflects premature mitotic entry after G2 abrogation
Survivin downregulation in virtual cell indicates increased apoptosis with checkpoint inhibition
ERBB3 upregulation in virtual cell and PI3K-inhibitor similarity suggest RTK/PI3K dependence
MYC downregulation in virtual cell; MYC-driven replication stress increases Chk1 dependence
Chk2 loss impairs DNA damage signaling and HR, complementing Chk1 inhibition
ATM pathway defects reduce DNA repair and increase reliance on Chk1
FOXO4 upregulation in virtual cell may reflect stress response and survival signaling
AURKA upregulation in virtual cell indicates mitotic stress and checkpoint vulnerability
